name: Dr Richard Davies
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: He embraces sex-positivity, neurodivergence and is LGBTQIA+ inclusive. Richard has experience working in the not-for-profit and private sectors of mental health, supporting young adults through to older persons presenting with mental health issues including; difficulties arising from negative thoughts, feelings and bodily sensations; recovery from trauma, neglect and abuse; relationship issues; grief/loss and existential issues; self-confidence/esteem concerns and; anxiety issues, including panic and excessive worry. Richard also has extensive experience in supporting clients across a wide range of relational and sexual health concerns, including intimacy anxiety, navigating changes and transitions in relationships (including separation support and infidelity), sexual addiction, pornography addiction, erectile difficulties, and premature ejaculation.

name: Elizabeth Muscat
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Her practice is grounded in trauma-informed, attachment-based theory, and she values supporting clients holistically and within their broader life context. Elizabeth has a particular interest in supporting clients through a range of sexual and relational challenges, including sexual pain (such as vulvodynia, vaginismus, and dyspareunia), sexual health anxiety, desire and arousal dissatisfaction (including navigating desire differences and erectile difficulties), orgasm-related difficulties (such as anorgasmia, orgasmic anhedonia, and premature ejaculation), and helping clients feel sexually empowered and confident.

name: Ellie Mackey
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Ellie has worked across school and public mental health settings, including facilitating psychoeducational talks for school groups and supporting individuals and communities following traumatic grief and critical incidents. She has experience in, and is passionate about supporting adults across a broad range of concerns, including mood and anxiety difficulties, low self-esteem, sleep difficulties, obsessions and compulsions, panic symptoms, Bipolar Disorder, body image issues, pre- and postnatal mental health, chronic illness and pain, stress and burnout, trauma (including PTSD and complex PTSD, childhood and adult sexual trauma, recent trauma, and relational/attachment trauma), grief and loss, and navigating life transitions. Ellie also has experience supporting clients across a wide range of intimacy and sexual health areas, including intimacy anxiety, navigating relationship changes and challenges (including transitions, dissatisfaction, separation, and infidelity), pre- and post-pregnancy support, LGBTQIA+ support, and those seeking sexual education. She has a special interest in working with those experiencing sexual pain (i.e., vulvodynia, vaginismus, and dyspareunia), sexual health anxiety, sexual addiction, desire and arousal dissatisfaction (including erectile difficulties and navigating libido differences) and orgasm-related difficulties (such as anorgasmia, orgasmic anhedonia, and premature ejaculation).

name: Emma Blanchard
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Emma is a trauma-informed and neuro-affirming psychologist who strives to create a safe, non-judgemental and self-compassionate space. She has experience working alongside clients with complex physical and mental health challenges and psychosocial disabilities, including chronic pain, complex trauma, Intellectual Disabilities, Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD), panic attacks and psychotic symptoms. Emma has a long history of community engagement in volunteering roles to support the LGBTQIA+ and non-monogamous communities, as well involvement in social justice activism. Emma is passionate about supporting clients from LGBTQIA+, rainbow family, and non-monogamous communities.

name: Emma McGregor
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Emma’s approach is neurodiversity-affirming, queer-inclusive and trauma-informed. This might be through reconnecting to desire, building assertiveness skills, neuroqueering relationship concepts, exploring sensory experiences, and making space for curiosity around sexuality (including exploration of the asexuality spectrum). Emma has experience in supporting clients across a wide range of relational and sexual health concerns, including intimacy and sexual health anxiety, navigating changes and transitions in relationships, sexual pain (i.e., vulvodynia, vaginismus, dyspareunia), desire and arousal dissatisfaction (including navigating libido differences and erectile difficulties), and orgasm-related difficulties (i.e., anorgasmia and orgasmic anhedonia). She also has experience providing affirming support for LGBTIQA+ individuals, those in non-monogamous relationships, sex workers, and clients seeking sexual education.
specialties: lgbtiqa+, queer, sex, sexual, sexuality, trauma

name: Jasmin Quinsee
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Jasmin is passionate about breaking down the shame/stigma surrounding sex and sexuality, whilst increasing practitioners and client’s ability to have vulnerable conversations in these spaces. She is sex positive, LGBTIAQ+ inclusive, kink and diverse relationship structure friendly and sex work positive. Inclusive of diverse relational structures (such as polyamory and non-monogamy) and sexual practices (such as kink). Sex is a space of great vulnerability for most and Jasmin creates and holds a safe space for individuals and their partner/s to talk about sex.
specialties: gender affirming, kink, lgbtiaq+, sex, sexual, sexuality, trauma

name: Jay McCabe
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: He has significant experience and is passionate about supporting LGBTQIA+ and neurodivergent clients through complex trauma, grief, depression, anxiety, and relationship issues, supporting them in their journey to become their authentic and unapologetic selves. Jay has a strong interest in working with individuals experiencing intimacy anxiety, sexual anxiety and relationship dissatisfaction including separation support. Please note that Jay also has experience supporting clients in a range of other mental and sexual health areas beyond what’s listed here.

name: Juliette Kingsford
title: Psychologist
practice: Sexual Health and Intimacy Psychological Services - East Brunswick Village
description: Juliette is neurodiversity affirming, sex positive, LGBTQIA+ inclusive, and kink and poly friendly. Juliette has experience in supporting clients across a wide range of relational and sexual health concerns, including intimacy anxiety, navigating changes and transitions in relationships (including separation support and infidelity), sexual pain (i.e., vulvodynia, vaginismus, dyspareunia), desire and arousal dissatisfaction (including navigating libido differences and erectile difficulties), and premature ejaculation. She also has experience providing affirming support for LGBTIQA+ individuals, those engaged in kink and non-monogamous relationships, sex workers, and clients seeking sexual education. Juliette has worked with clients that have experienced recent and historical trauma, attachment disruptions, disconnections amongst family members, grief, symptoms of depression and anxiety, and clients who are exploring their sexual and gender identities.
specialties: kink, lgbtiqa+, lgbtqia+, sex, sexual, trauma
